incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High error rate observed for routing service (route-engine) — paging oncall maya (oncall). Incident ID: INC-2026-2243

maya (oncall): acked — I'm on it. looking at routing metrics now.

maya (oncall): @jon can you pull recent smart-routing logs? seeing a spike in 502/504 from edge proxies.

jon (eng-sre): pulling logs: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z route-engine[router-12] ERROR upstream_connect_failure: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.200.5.12:8080
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z route-engine[router-12] WARN fallback: selecting fallback pool eu-west-1-b because primary endpoint missing
2026-03-15T14:02:13Z route-engine[router-12] INFO proxy_send: 504 gateway_timeout to client
```

jon (eng-sre): looks like the edge VIPs for eu-west-1 are resolving to stale endpoints in some POPs which then immediately trigger a fallback to another region -> creates a loop where fallback then times out and gets retried.

priya (dns): I can confirm a partial DNS propagation lag. our authoritative nodes show mixed A records for vip-edge.redwood.io across regions. TTL was 300 but we had a manual change ~20m ago.

priya (dns): dig from two locations: 
```
# from us-east-1
$ dig +short vip-edge.redwood.io @ns1.redwood.net
10.10.10.5
# from eu-west-1
$ dig +short vip-edge.redwood.io @ns1.redwood.net
10.200.5.12
# cached reply in edge POP (asia)
10.10.10.5
```

maya (oncall): so some POPs still have old IPs that are dead/unroutable -> route-engine tries primary -> fails -> policy fallback to eu-west-1-b which also has inconsistent endpoints -> oscillation.

liam (runtime): also seeing model-variant mismatch in logs when fallback picks different pool: requests get routed to a smaller variant (gpt-small-q) that doesn't support current request shape, causing 422s mixed in with 504s.

ella (support): Customer impact: several enterprise tenants reported increased latency and failed generations starting ~13:58 UTC. Support tickets #4721/#4723. Not widespread but several high-traffic customers hit errors.

maya (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) pause smart-routing fallbacks, 2) force ring to warm pool in safe region, 3) purge edge DNS cache where possible, 4) reduce DNS TTLs for authoritative zone.

jon (eng-sre): executing: `routectl set-policy --name SRT_POLICY_v2 --fallback disabled` — applying now.

jon (eng-sre): policy disabled. telemetry shows fallback rate dropping from 18% -> 2% in 20s.

priya (dns): changing TTL to 60s and adding a sync push to secondaries. `dnsctl zone update vip-edge.redwood.io --ttl 60` done. pushing SOA increment.

priya (dns): issuing edge purge command for known POPs: `edge-purge --target vip-edge.redwood.io --pops eu-west-1,ap-southeast-1` — started.

liam (runtime): warm-pool routing: moving traffic to dedicated warm hosts in eu-west-1-a: `runtimectl route-override --vip vip-edge.redwood.io --force-host 10.200.5.20` — applied. health checks green.

maya (oncall): monitoring error rate and customer complaints. @ella, coordinate with support to update affected customers: advise retry with exponential backoff; we're disabling fallbacks to avoid oscillation.

ella (support): will post an update to affected customers in #support-alerts and create a short incident blurb.

jon (eng-sre): graph shows p50 latency returning to normal, p95 still elevated but trending down. fallback churn metric flattened.

priya (dns): note: some third-party DNS resolvers may keep old answers until their cache TTL expires. reducing our TTL helps but can't force remote caches.

maya (oncall): next actions: - keep SRT_POLICY_v2 fallback disabled for 30m - continue DNS TTL 60 and monitor - schedule a controlled rollback of the manual change that triggered this once propagation confirmed - postmortem owner: jon, dns owner: priya, runtime owner: liam.

liam (runtime): I'll also add a guard in route-engine so fallback selection requires endpoint health probe pass >2 consecutive checks before switching. Will open PR now.

jon (eng-sre): adding a short-term alert: fire if fallback rate >5% for 5m after re-enable.

maya (oncall): can we re-enable fallback in safe mode? maybe phased by POPs.

priya (dns): let's wait one TTL cycle (~60s * 5 to be conservative) then re-evaluate. I'll update when secondaries confirm consistent records.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-2243 acknowledged by maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): summary for now: root cause = manual DNS IP update + 300s TTL + partial propagation + route-engine fallback policy that aggressively fails over to different region without health check hysteresis -> led to routing oscillation and model-variant mismatch. Impact = localized customer errors and elevated latency for some tenants. Mitigation = disabled fallbacks, reduced TTL, edge purge, forced warm pool routing. Owners assigned for follow-up.

ella (support): support message drafted and queued. I'll add known affected customers list.

jon (eng-sre): I'll start the postmortem doc and include timeline + commands executed and PR link for fallback guard.

priya (dns): I'll run a full audit of recent DNS changes and propose a safe-change checklist for VIP updates (include shorter TTL pre-warm window).

maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then hand off to day shift. paging cleared for now. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-2243 updated: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, owners=[jon, priya, liam]

maya (oncall): handoff to jon at 15:12 UTC if still stable.

jon (eng-sre): acknowledged handoff. I'll follow up with postmortem and remediation tasks.

ella (support): closing customer interim tickets after confirmation. will await postmortem before final external comms.

maya (oncall): last check: error_rate=0.8% (baseline 0.2%), p95 latency down to 420ms. marking thread resolved in 30m if stable.
